Guardrails.title: Zero warnings. Everything is an error.
Guardrails.subtitle: Strict rules baked into every scaffold. Your agent can't deviate — lint and typecheck catch violations instantly.
Guardrails.eslint: Errors only, no warnings. Every rule enforces. No eslint-disable allowed.
Guardrails.typescript: Strict mode, no any, no ts-ignore. Type guards at boundaries.
Guardrails.convex: Dual validators, bounded reads, withIndex for queries. No full table scans.
Guardrails.zero_error: Every scaffold passes lint + typecheck + build out of the box. If it doesn't, it's a CLI bug.

Doctor.title: Preflight for every change
Doctor.subtitle: vllnt doctor validates project health and surfaces issues with structured fix commands your agent can execute directly.

Agents.title: Works with your AI coding agent
Agents.subtitle: Every scaffolded project ships with optimized rules for the leading AI coding agents. Your agent understands the architecture from the first prompt.

Manifesto.title: Why I'm building this
Manifesto.subtitle: An open letter from the creator of create-vllnt-app.
Manifesto.p1: I've spent years building products — web apps, mobile apps, fullstack systems. Every new project started the same way: days of boilerplate, weeks of configuration, and the constant feeling that I was solving the same problems over and over.
Manifesto.p2: Then AI coding agents arrived. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Windsurf — they changed everything. Suddenly I could ship 10x faster. But there was a catch: these agents are only as good as the context you give them. Drop an AI agent into a blank project and it flounders. Drop it into a well-structured project with clear rules, conventions, and architecture docs, and it becomes a 100x multiplier.
Manifesto.p3: That's the insight behind create-vllnt-app. It's not just a scaffolder — it's the bridge between your idea and a project that AI agents can immediately understand and extend. CLAUDE.md files with blocking rules. AGENTS.md with architecture diagrams. Cursor and Windsurf rules derived from the same source of truth. Documentation that serves both humans and machines.
Manifesto.p4: This scaffolder is deliberately opinionated. Next.js for web. Expo for mobile. Convex for the backend. Tailwind for styling. Feature-sliced architecture. These aren't arbitrary choices — they're the stack I've battle-tested across dozens of production apps. When your AI agent knows the stack, it writes better code. When the conventions are consistent, the agent makes fewer mistakes.
Manifesto.h_open: Open source because it has to be
Manifesto.p5: create-vllnt-app is open source because the best developer tools always are. I want every solo developer, every indie hacker, every small team to have the same scaffolding advantage that I do. Fork it, extend it, make it yours. The templates are just the starting point.
Manifesto.p6: We're at the beginning of a fundamental shift in how software gets built. The developers who win will be the ones who learn to work with AI agents, not against them. That means structuring projects for AI comprehension, writing rules that prevent common mistakes, and building scaffolds that give agents the context they need from the first prompt.
Manifesto.p7: That's what create-vllnt-app is: a head start on the future of development.
